utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-67-R77.3-T, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before I call for the appearances, I note for the record that we sit under Rule 15 bis this afternoon, Judge Kwon being absent. Yes. May we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I'm Bruce MacFarlane, an attorney from Canada, and have been appointed as the amicus curiae to prosecute the case. And with me this afternoon and throughout these proceedings is Lori Ann Wanlin, also an attorney from Canada.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. And, Mr. Seselj, you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Dr. Vojislav Seselj, a university professor, and the principal enemy of The Hague Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Seselj. So noted. Before we begin, can we go into private session. There is a ruling the Chamber has to deliver.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. I have a question. I asked you a minute ago if I may put the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Judge, I would kindly ask you to note that I had not asked for any protective measures to be granted. Three years ago, I gave a statement which was verified by this Court. There are other documents as well that contain my full name, my address. And by virtue of this document, my name is now in the public domain. I don't know why I should be now testifying under protective measures, because everybody knows my first and last name. I don't see any reason for that. So I disclosed this when I testified first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Your observations have been noted, sir. And as I would have explained to Mr. Seselj, who has called you as a witness, before you came into the court, it is not for us to remove those -- rescind those protective measures. They have been granted by another Trial Chamber in other proceedings, and it is entirely possible that those protective measures could be removed, but it would have to be done by the Chamber who imposed it. Only that Chamber, at this point, is competent to rescind those measures. Before I invite Mr. Seselj to begin, I would point out - and you having testified previously before the Tribunal, would be familiar with the procedure - that the side calling you, in this case Mr. Seselj, would begin by asking you questions, and after which Mr. MacFarlane, who is to your left, would be -- sorry, to your right, who appears as the Amicus Prosecutor in this matter, would have an opportunity to cross-examine you. And the Judges may have questions for you at any point. And with that, I would invite Mr. Seselj to begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Mr. DS-1 - I have to address you in that way, completely contrary to my will - can you tell me what is your profession?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you work for the police during the war from 1991 to 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Were you ever a member of the Serbian Chetnik Movement or the Serbian Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was a sympathiser of the Chetnik -- Serbian Chetnik Movement, because it wasn't registered at the time. Later, I organised some of my units. From the end of 1991 until the end of 1993, I was a member of the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note: Could the speakers please pause between questions and answers. Interpreters cannot cope at this pace.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj and Mr. Witness, I would ask you to bear in mind that what you say has to be interpreted. So in addition to pacing yourselves so that the interpreters can keep up, allow a gap between the question and the witness's attempt to answer. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You said that from 1991, autumn of 1991, until autumn of 1993, you were a member of the Serbian Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: During that period, did you have any position in the Serbian Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: None?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then in the autumn of 1993, why did you leave the Serbian Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was expelled from the Radical Serbian Party in 1993. Mr. Subotic wrote a letter to the leadership of the Serbian Radical Party, accusing me of carrying grenades around Srebrenica, which is absolutely untrue because that is something I never did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, let us distinguish two things. There was one accusation, that you were walking around the town wearing a grenade at your belt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And that was the reason for your expulsion from the party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But now you said that that wasn't true, that you didn't carry this grenade, and that you were expelled for no reasons at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, let us leave aside the grounds of your expulsion, whether they were justified or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Please slow down so the interpreters can keep up with you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Hall, I thought that I slowed down, but I will slow down even further.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So we made the distinction between these two things, the reasons for your expulsion and what you claim, that that was completely unfounded because it was untrue and there was no reason for your expulsion. Do you know that you can file a request for reconsideration of this decision whenever you wish to do so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You were not interested in doing that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, this decision about your expulsion, based on the accusation that you walked around the town with a grenade at your belt, demonstrates that the Serbian Radical Party was against the practice of its members carrying any kind of weapons when in town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. At the time, I worked as a policeman, and I am familiar with the situation. I never saw a single member of the Radical Party carrying a gun, a grenade, or any kind of weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you take part in the war in the former federal unit of Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you ever go there as a volunteer of the Serbian Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Once.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To Skelani.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Skelani, on the Drina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That's near Bajina Basta, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the other bank of the Drina River?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Where else did you go to the front not as a member of the Serbian Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went to Slavonia and Bosnia on several occasions. I was in contact with TO people, and wherever humanitarian need was required, that was what we provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How many times did you go to the front without the mediation of the Serbian Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Four or five times.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: This one time when you went in the organisation of the Serbian Radical Party, where did you set off from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you remember where from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that we reported at the Serbian Radical Party offices in Ohridska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was that the headquarters of the party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you see me then, on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And where did you go after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We boarded civilian buses, and we went to Bubanj Potok, where we were met by officers of the regular army, who gave us identical clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Trial Chamber what Bubanj Potok is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's a military facility for training.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is it a barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it's not a barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What is it, then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's a training exercise ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: May I have a moment, please. We have the pseudonym sheet to which I referred prepared, which I would invite the Usher to pass to the witness, and he can sign it if he is satisfied that its accurate.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, it is my first and last name. But this "DS-1," do I have to sign that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: That is the pseudonym that has been assigned to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: If you're satisfied with the date of birth and your name, you may sign it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do I have to sign it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Witness, I suggest you sign, not to waste more time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise for wasting time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The most important thing here for myself and the Judges is your testimony here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but this "DS-1," well ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Show it to counsel. So that should be entered as an exhibit and marked accordingly.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D1, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, let's round off this introductory portion of the examination. Answer this, please: During the war from 1991 to 1995, did you ever meet me anywhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the first time that I see you close up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The first time in your life that you see me in person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. In this way, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, when did you have the first contacts with the representatives of The Hague OTP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first contact was in 2002, when Mrs. Natasa Kandic or - how shall I call her? - she came to where I lived, the place I lived, and asked me if I was so and so, and whether I had been to the war, and whether I'd heard about you, and whether I'd heard about Milosevic, the late president, and then she gave me -- well, actually, she threatened me and said that an indictment would be raised against me at this Tribunal if I failed to contact the investigators of The Hague Tribunal, co-operate with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And when did you have this contact with the investigators?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Soon after that, a man came to see me with a jeep, and he had diplomatic number plates. I remember that. He introduced himself as Paolo Pastore, and he took me to a location in Novi Sad, to an office there of a lady lawyer, Olivera Franicevic was her name - and he questioned me with regard to the battle-field and he wrote this down on his laptop, and said -- and what is it he wanted to know?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What else did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said that if I failed to testify in The Hague, that a criminal report would be raised against me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Who were you asked to testify against in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Against you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Only against me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And against Slobodan Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I see. Now, could you explain what these threats involved? What were they like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. But let me say that a few months before that, I had a very serious operation, and half my abdomen was cut out, so I was in a very poor state indeed. But, anyway, he said that they had all the proof they needed against me or all the evidence against me, saying that I had committed crimes on the territory of the Republic of Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina that I know nothing about. And in the health state that I was in, I accepted. I didn't know what else to do. I had nobody to discuss this with, the authorities being what they were, so I agreed. They were DOS authorities, so I agreed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you sign a statement of any kind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not at that particular moment, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And when did you sign the statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They called me to come to Belgrade, and I was there for three days afterwards, at the offices of The Hague Tribunal - I think that's what they were - and for three days they wrote statements, because he dictated. He said it wasn't essential for me to say that I had heard anything. I heard things via television, the information media and in the newspapers. What was important for him was that I should say that I had seen it all, seen what he was writing and dictating.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, can you tell us specifically what these events were, whether they were real events or constructed events?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, specifically, I can give you the example of one particular situation, and that was the sole time that I went to Skelani in the Serbian Radical Party. He said, well, that you had issued some orders that the Muslims and children in their cradles should be killed, that everybody should be slaughtered, and that there were some police generals there and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When you went to Skelani, to the battle-front, was it your task to protect the dam there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The dam on the Drina River?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, did you tell this man, Stocchi, how can I say that was the order when there were no Muslims living there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, of course I told him that, and the second instance was when he mentioned the Catholic cathedral in Subotica, that it was mined.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, was that in the statement, that I mined the cathedral or my men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Paolo wrote that, although I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did it say that it was blown up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's what he wrote down. He said pursuant to your orders, and that was the dictation he gave, that pursuant to your orders, members of the Serbian Radical Party mined the Subotica cathedral, and I remember that very well. However, I worked in the police force myself, and I passed by the cathedral on a daily basis -- and the individual who did that was not a Serb, to begin with. The cathedral was not mined. I don't know if the doors were damaged, but that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Can you remember the Muslim who damaged the cathedral --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly slow down and pause between question and answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The interpreters are reminding you to slow down and pause between question and answer. Yes, Mr. MacFarlane.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you. If I might intervene at this stage. I've not intervened at this point because I recognised that the accused was leading through some introductory materials. But it appears that he's now moving in another direction. My concern is that I fail to see the relevance of the evidence, in terms of the order in lieu of indictment. The factual issues, the issues in this case, are not being touched at all by this witness. And if the accused wishes to quickly move into areas that are directly relevant to the order in lieu of indictment, that's fine, but we're way off on the side, on an off-ramp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. MacFarlane. Mr. Seselj, I don't think that I could improve on the language that Mr. MacFarlane has just used. So bearing in mind what this trial is concerned with, could you confine the evidence that you are leading to the issues in this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Hall, I assume you have been informed that I had planned 60 minutes for this witness. We've already been talking for 10 minutes, and we're still on the introduction. Now, for us to get through the basic subject of this trial exhaustively, you have to be aware of the general circumstances. I did not dwell on details. What I'm trying to do is to have a dialogue with this witness and to paint a picture of the general circumstances to you, which are extremely important; why, for example, it was so important for me to see that the statement provided to me by this witness be made public, with his agreement, of course. I think you ought to know all that so that you can rule correctly in this case. Otherwise, there would be no need of holding this trial at all. You could make your judgement and sentence on the basis of general information. But I am getting to the crux of the matter, but I do need to receive a bit more information.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When you had this talk with -- this interview with Stocchi, how did you feel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, as I say, I was a sick man and I was under threat; the DOS power and authority. I couldn't feel well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did they offer you residence in a third country if you accepted to testify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of course, that I should confirm everything we'd agreed upon, and if I did that, I would be taken to third countries.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did they accept that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And where were you?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What was your testimony like in the Milosevic trial?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it was like this: I was there. We had a month's preparation, roughly speaking, telling me what I was to say in court. And the agreement was that I should look at the Judge, Judge May, I think his name was, and to the right of me we had Mr. Daniel Saxon, who gave me signals. So sometimes I had to look to my right. And then if I wasn't saying something that they expected me to say, they would interrupt the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, did you testify truthfully in that trial?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I testified what had been written, so I testified falsely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Falsely? Were you forced to testify falsely?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was forced to testify falsely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Your Honours, we haven't improved at all, and now we're into testimony in another trial almost 10 years ago, with allegations of signals from the Prosecutor. I really don't know where this is going. The issues for this case are clear, and they relate to protective measures, and breaches of those protective measures, and a book that was published. I urge the Chamber to direct the accused to ensure that his questions and the answers are directed to those issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, you wanted to say something?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Judge. Now that the gentleman said - I forget his name - said what he just said, let me tell you one thing, something else that came prior to that. First of all, I was treated here, and it was not suitable treatment. They took me to a doctor who heard that I was a Serb and didn't want to treat me, provide me with medical treatment. So under threats from Daniel Saxon, Paolo Pastore Stocchi, Ms. Hilary [as interpreted] and Richard Nice. The second time, they pulled my teeth out here in The Hague and gave me Valium, and then they interviewed me for Mr. Seselj and Milosevic. I hope this will be made public, because so far I haven't had a chance to say this in public.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, may I be allowed to say something, please?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: As I was about to say --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please. Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry. Coming back to Mr. MacFarlane's objection, when --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to say something in that regard. Judges, you are here as the guardians of international justice. And as the guardians of international justice, it is incumbent upon you -- it is much more important for you to hear what the witness said here loud and clear in this courtroom, where he said that he testified -- was forced to testify falsely in the Milosevic trial than this whole case against me. That is a much more important fact, and I think you should reject Mr. MacFarlane's interventions. Were he a real lawyer, he would like to reach the truth, and not to have these petty intrusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Seselj, the case against you is a discrete case, in the sense of the contempt we're dealing with. And whilst I can understand readily that someone has a burning issue to say something, there are other places and other forae in which they can say it, if they wish to do so, without saying it here. And it's much better to all parties we simply stick to what is truly relevant that you have to extract from the witness by way of defence to this charge. The other thing is this: that when two fluent people are speaking one to the other, it's inevitable that you engage in a conversation, and conversations get more and more rapid, and the interpreters are going to left further and further behind. It's not easy, but please remember to try and put a gap in between the questions and the answers, because at the moment you're overlapping. And though the interpreters do a very good job, miracles are outside their pay grade, I should think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge. Yes, Mr. Seselj, please continue with your relevant questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I believe that my questions so far have been more than relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And what was your monthly income in the Netherlands?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it was around 700 Euros.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On a monthly basis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But you had been provided with every other necessity; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So two and a half thousand Euros. Do you remember what was the average wage in Serbia in 2004 and 2005?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How much?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Around 10 Euros.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: No, no, no, 2004 or 2005.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you fled Norway because you refused to testify against me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How did my team, supporting my defence, contact you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After I returned to Serbia, I kept a sort of low profile, and I had to do that primarily because of my illness and the operation that I had undergone. But as soon as I was getting better and I was socialising much with members of the Radical Party, I asked them to arrange a contact for me with Petar Jojic from your Defence team. I knew him personally. I called him, I told him who I was, and I offered to give a statement because I wanted to tell everything that I'm trying to say today, but I have been interrupted so many times. I have this statement with me here, and I can present that to the Judges. So that was the statement given on the 19th of April, 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You actually gave a number of statements to my Defence support team?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Let's just clear up one point. I may be wrong about this, and that's why I'm seeking the witness's clarification. You've referred to somebody you've named as Mr. Richard Nice. Do you mean that or do you mean Mr. Geoffrey Nice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Geoffrey Nice, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you, yourself, insist on having all the statements that you gave to my Defence support team to be public?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And did you also appear in the Serbian print media in that context?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you give interviews?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you present the facts that we have highlighted here about your false testimony in the Milosevic case, about the pressure for you to testify falsely? Did you present all these facts in those interviews?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did, but I provided more details.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Those were extensive interviews?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they contained my full name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Can you remember any newspaper that you gave an interview to; for example, "Pravda," the 28th of April -- 24 April, 2008.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and the Court can look at it and can see that my name was disclosed in public.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It is in the hands of the Trial Chamber to decide that. Did you publish your interviews in the newspapers before your statement given to my associate was published in one of my books?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the speakers please pause between questions and answers. It is impossible to interpret at this pace.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, the same point again. The interpreters are complaining about the speed of the conversation, and particularly the lack of a pause between the questions and answers. I know it's easy to run away with this, and I know you're not doing it deliberately, but make a conscious effort to slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to repeat my question, although I was convinced that I was speaking slowly enough. Now I'm going to speak even more slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did my associates ask you if you agreed for your statement, given to my Defence team, to be publicised in one of my books?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, that's what I literally said to the Defence team. I gave them permission to use it for any purpose that they would like to do so. It could be used in newspapers, in your books, on the internet. So I gave them a free hand as to the use of my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, your statements given to my team, were they written in such a manner that they clearly indicate your will to be my witness, my witness for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. And any time in the future, should you need me to come here, I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you refuse publicly to appear as a Prosecution defence [as interpreted] against me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I refused. I didn't want to do that at any cost.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you use similar words when you appeared in public in meetings, in rallies in Serbia, organised with a view to protecting my legal rights?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I appeared, let's say, at at least 10 or a dozen meetings or promotions of your books that were held in Serbia. In September of last year, I wasn't able to attend because I had some heart problem, but via a videolink, I gave a statement containing all my personal details, which was watched by more than 7.000 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When you appeared in the public for the first time with your statements to the effect that you gave a false testimony in the Slobodan Milosevic case under the duress and threats from The Hague OTP, and when, for the first time through your newspaper interviews, you imparted to the public that you had refused to appear as a false witness for the Prosecution in the proceedings conducted against me, from that moment on, that is to say, once your identity was disclosed by your own volition, did you encounter any problems?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Never. I'm socialising with people and going out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you receive any threatening telephone or nuisance calls?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Were you or your family threatened in any way whatsoever, in the street, at your work-place, anywhere, concerning your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not on the part of the Radicals, but, yes, on the part of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What kind of problems did you have with the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In addition to my heart problems, because I have three bypasses and had undergone other surgeries, the OTP people gave instructions to the doctors in Sremska Kamenica to do the catheterisation of my heart, which means to open up my heart, to insert a catheter into my heart which had already been operated on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That is called ablatio, isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know it's called catheterisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You heard I had undergone the same procedure last year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I hope you don't mind, but I'm going to put a direct question to you in order to avoid being suggestive. Would you agree that we discussed in more detail your health condition in 2003 and 2004?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But before that, let me ask you this: Were you called to appear as a witness of the Trial Chamber in the proceedings against me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I refused that, and I have papers to prove that. And I refused every time they did so, and I'm going to do the same in the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, if the Trial Chamber would allow me, you refused to become as a Prosecution witness, but if I remember correctly, you did agree to appear as a Trial Chamber witness. But after that, you were examined by a medical commission, who stated that you were not capable of coming?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe I don't understand all the terminology involved, but I passed a message to Mr. Antonetti that it was only you who could call me to appear as a witness. It was Judge Antonetti who ordered the medical team to carry out a medical examination in order to establish my health condition in Sremska Kamenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And what did they find out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They found out that I was incapable of appearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Correct me if I'm wrong, but you agreed to testify via videolink, but that was also banned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was prohibited from doing that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I hope we shall have enough time to go briefly through the events that took place during your 18 months' stay in the Netherlands prior to your testimony in the Slobodan Milosevic case. So I can speak openly about all the ailments you're suffering from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You don't mind at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 7th of February, you had a problem with a stomach hernia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you were taken to a surgeon on the 7th of February, 2003. The doctor decided that you needed an operation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Then on the 14th of February, did you have severe pain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that was a heart problem that I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was the emergency doctor called in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In order to facilitate this for the Trial Chamber, and also for the Amicus Prosecutor, this is a review I received from the Prosecutor in the main case. This is the information that I received from which I extracted these basic facts, so you can check with the OTP whether these facts are true or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You also had an attack of anxiety on the 14th of September?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that was all due to the heart condition.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And strong analgesics were prescribed to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Then you had a gastroscopic examination?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, of my stomach.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 23rd of February, you had blood in your urine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And your supposition was that that was caused by your left kidney?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Then on the 24th of February, you visited a GP, who gave you a referral for a urologist?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 25th of February, you visited a urologist --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Haven't we again moved into irrelevancies, in terms of these issues?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Hall, please trust me as if I were the best lawyer at the high Tribunal. All of this makes sense, and at the very end you will be sure to realise what the relevance and the point is. Just please be patient, and you will see that I am right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I would only remind you that the 60 minutes you had indicated you had for this witness, you have 25 minutes left. So if you use more time than that, of course, it would have to be adjusted, in terms of the other witnesses that you intend to call. Yes, Mr. MacFarlane.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: I raise the same question of relevancy again. But in addition, I have noted in the last 10 or 15 minutes that the accused is increasingly leading the witness and providing a fair bit of information to the witness in his questions. I'm sure that the Chamber will give appropriate weight to that, but I'm concerned about that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, that did occur to me as well, Mr. MacFarlane. But inasmuch as the issues appeared irrelevant, it wasn't -- I thought that he was leading up to something. Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Hall, this will definitely bring us somewhere. These are the facts that can easily be verifiable in the Tribunal against all the dates that I cited, so there is no leading here. Who could have remembered all these dates? Neither the witness, nor I. So all of this is noted down and contained in the Tribunal documents. There is no dispute about that. We are not disputing any facts or any hearsay that was mentioned in the testimony. All of this has been documented and duly noted in the OTP and The Hague Tribunal documentation. And I hope, Mr. Hall, that you are going to reduce the time wasted by the Prosecutor's interventions. Otherwise, I won't be able to finish my examination in 60 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So 25th of February, an X-ray of your kidneys?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And your urine samples were taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 26th of February, did you undergo gastroscopy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was a sample of the stomach taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was it when those helico-bacteria were detected that caused ulcers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you have presurgery examination on the 4th of March by an anesthesiologist?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 6th of March, were you told that you had a surgery scheduled for the 19th of March?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And were you, indeed, operated on the 19th of March?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think so, but I don't know about the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you complain on the 28th of March of pains in your legs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 31st of March, did they take out your stitches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The physician, on the 24th of April, did he consider that one of your stitches had burst?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember, but probably, yes. I don't have any documentation about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 28th of April, did you have a cystoscopic examination?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 20th of May, did you go and see the urologist once again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 16th of June, did you have severe toothache?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did the dentist prescribe analgesics and penicillin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 24th of June, did the dentist extract the tooth in question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, that's what I just said: Not just one tooth; more teeth.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, he extracted one tooth and then had a plan for the rest of your teeth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and he pulled all my teeth out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you provide an electromyogram from Serbia, according to which you suffered from polyneuropathy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is from -- poisoning from noxious matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 24th of June, was another of your teeth extracted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether he extracted them one by one or more than one on one day. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, did you have even more severe problems after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 27th of June, did the dentist observe that when another dentist extracted your tooth, your sinus canal was impaired?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but they skipped some data there, because they took me to see a dentist here and he gave me Valium, he prescribed Valium, and then pulled my teeth out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Now, on the 1st of July, did the dentist extract -- remove your stitches and clean your other teeth, the rest of your teeth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you have an EMG examination on the 2nd of July?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 16th of July, did you again complain of toothache when the dentist opened up the tooth that had created all the problems to begin with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 7th of July -- or, rather, the 17th of July, did you go and see the neurologist?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He prescribed an anti-depressive, together with an analgesic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 21st of July, did you have pain in your -- suffer pain in your legs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you were prescribed some pills?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 5th of August, did you go to see an oral surgeon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And he prescribed some antibiotics; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: For the sinus canal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 7th of August, did you go and see the oral surgeon again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because my jaw was infected as a result of the interventions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Another dentist, on the 20th of August, did he prepare caps for your teeth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 26th of August, did you go for an MRI examination in a hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 2nd of September, did you go and see the oral surgeon again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And they took an imprint of your jaw and teeth for a prosthesis, and then you went to see a neurologist because of back pains; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 10th of September, did you go and see a neurologist because of poisoning by gas?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 11th of September, did you go and see the dentist again, who put a cap on your tooth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 17th of September, did you have another check-up at the dentist?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 23rd of September, did they extract your front teeth and supply you with a prosthesis, with dentures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, how was it, then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I said, there was allegedly a dentist here that they took me to see, and he extracted all my teeth in the upper jaw at the same time, not one by one. Then the wound was infected, and then another dentist had to intervene.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then the dentures didn't agree with you, and they had to do them again; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 20th of October, did you suffer strong pain and couldn't get out of bed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You were given medicaments again, analgesics, pills for your stomach and something to calm you down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was because of my heart.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And on the 20th of October, did you go and see the dentist again because you had problems with your lower dentures, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 3rd of November, you had problems with rheumatism and had a medical examination; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 13th of November, did you go and see a general practitioner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did, I went to see a GP. I don't know what date that was exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 1st of December, did you start acupuncture treatment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, when I last intervened, you indicated you were leading us somewhere. I confess I'm still having difficulty understanding the relevance of all of this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please trust me this time, Mr. Hall. And if it doesn't prove to be correct, then I won't do the same thing with the next. But please bear with me for just a little while longer. Do you agree to do so? You do agree, but unwillingly, I gather.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 3rd of December -- on the 3rd of December, did you undergo acupuncture treatment again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then on the 8th of December again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 15th of December?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the 17th of December?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then the Tribunal paid for two weeks of herbal treatment; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, with some Chinese preparations.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 29th of November, once again, acupuncture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It was a month-long therapy with several sessions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 17th of February, you underwent six more treatment sessions, is that right, on the 19th of February, and then you asked for more pills on the 24th of February before you were transferred to another country; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did provide me with some medicaments.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 25th -- or, rather, on the 25th of March, did you go and see the dentist again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And this dentist checked your dentures and adjusted them so that you felt better with them; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And he said that you had to be fitted with a new denture for your lower jaw; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 6th of April, did you have some more problems? You weren't able to sleep because you were suffering from pain in your legs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you have pain in your urinary tract?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And did you have an infection of some kind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Possibly. I suffered from a cold, and possibly that, too, but I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In April, May, and June 2004, did you undergo regular acupuncture sessions again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 17th of May, did you go and see the dentist again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably. As I say, I can't remember the exact dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And did he devise a plan for you for the following month; to cap your teeth, to adjust your dentures, and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because I had problems with one of my teeth and the lower dentures, so I had to go several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 25th of June, did you collapse, did you faint, and your wife had to call the emergency services?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You felt pain in your chest, in the heart area and the neck area; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 26th of June, did you have a similar attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 1st of June, were you provided and fitted with a new lower denture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 3rd of June, did you go and see the doctor again because you fell off your bicycle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you ride your bicycle in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Ah-hah, I see. Now, on the 7th of July, 2004, was your upper denture adjusted again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: On the 2nd of September, did you go and see the doctor again because of your hernia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That, then, is a list of all your conditions and medical ailments. Now, I don't know if you've followed my trial, but for a year and a half I had great trouble here because they did not want to fit me with a new cap and bridge for my teeth, and my root was infected and pussy, and I have been suffering from that for a year and a half already here. And have you heard just how many problems The Hague detentionees have here at the detention centre? They try to save money and it's difficult to see doctors. Now, on the basis of this, you had privileged treatment, didn't you, quite obviously?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I said, yes, I had all this treatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Does that mean, then, that The Hague Tribunal counted on your false testimony in the Slobodan Milosevic trial a great deal, they set great store by it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but they didn't know about the fact that I presented in my statements, while I was preparing for the Milosevic trial, during the proofing sessions, I went out to light a cigarette. There was a break, and Mr. Daniel Saxon was present, and so was Ms. Hilary [as interpreted], I think her name was, and they said, Don't you worry, everything will be fine. All you have to do is confirm you are a participant in the events, and not say that you had heard about them or whatever. Milosevic won't leave alive -- won't leave the prison alive, nor will Mr. Seselj. I think that's enough of a threat, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, is it clear to you that Slobodan Milosevic had only 10 per cent of this kind of medical -- had he had only 10 per cent of this kind of medical care and attention, he would be alive today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So while they were counting on your false testimony, you were given all this extra care?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but I didn't have a single document, so I couldn't leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And when you refused to testify in my trial, then all you got were threats, a series of threats; is that the truth of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Mr. Hall, I hope you have understood why it was important for me to present all these facts and figures, and I have given all this information because of other people in the Hague Tribunal, because of General Vladimir Lazarevic, Jovica Stanisic, and many others who need medical care and protection which is being mostly withheld. However, when it is in the interests of The Hague OTP Office to provide the Tribunal with false witnesses for a trial, then everything is possible and there's enough money for everything. Jovica Stanisic can bleed the whole night in his cell without anybody paying any attention whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. At this point, we are hearing either submission or speeches, neither of which are acceptable.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I had to explain to you at the end what the point was, because you had interrupted me a few times because you didn't realise what I wanted to achieve. And I did, indeed, achieve what I wanted, with the co-operation of this witness, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Judge --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: You have used the forum of this trial to make a number of suggestions and allegations and whatnot, which may have some relevance elsewhere, but have nothing to do with the issues with which we are concerned. And, therefore, there is nothing that this Chamber, seized of the discrete question, as Judge Morrison has pointed out earlier, can do about those matters. But you took advantage of the forum, and it's gone out. I would only remind you that when we take the break in four minutes, you will have exhausted the -- the first break for the afternoon in four minutes' time - we will be breaking for thirty minutes - you will have exhausted the sixty minutes that you have for this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, Mr. Hall. I have just completed my examination-in-chief of this witness. I have saved a few minutes which I will, hopefully, be able to use with another witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask a question? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. What Mr. Seselj said about my health condition is true, but I would like to mention another event which I think was very important. During an examination in Zoetermeer, and I think it had to do with the poison -- poison gasses, the doctor asked the interpreter whether I was a Muslim. She shook her head. He asked whether I was a Croat. She shook her head. But when she confirmed that I was a Serb, the doctor says, Serves him right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, we're at the point where we're two minutes shy of when we intended to adjourn, but it would be convenient to break now. And Mr. MacFarlane would begin his cross-examination in 30 minutes, when we resume.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. MacFarlane.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Sir, in your evidence, you indicated at an early stage that you are a policeman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: How long have you been a policeman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From 1981 until 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: And so you are no longer a policeman at the moment; you finished that in 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Voluntarily, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: While you were a policeman in your home area, did you have occasion to go to court to testify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Did it happen to be in connection with crimes that you were investigating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Within the domain of police work; crime reports, misdemeanors reports. It depends.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: And you would appear, much like we have here today, with lawyers present and a judge or judges?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Similar. It's not quite this way. Those were regular proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Were you required to take an oath at the beginning of your evidence or give a solemn declaration to tell the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As a policeman, I spoke the truth, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: But that wasn't my question. My question was: Were you required to take an oath or to give a solemn declaration to tell the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it depended on the case involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Based on your experience testifying in your home area, and that on occasion you would be required to give an oath or to give a solemn declaration, you would, of course, understand the importance of telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course, and I'm glad to be here today to be able to tell the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: When you testified in the Milosevic trial, you indicated that you gave false testimony; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I testified as I was supposed to testify, as I was told to testify, as I was taught to testify, as was written up for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: That, unfortunately, doesn't answer my question. My question is whether or not you gave false evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was blackmailed with the possibility of charges being brought against me in this Court. The second time, when I was called for Mr. Seselj in 2005, I knew that no one could press charges against me any longer, and that is why I was in a position to tell the truth. And I have been telling the truth since the 1st of January, 2005; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Well, regrettably, you are, for whatever reason, not answering my question. My question is a very simple one, whether or not you gave false evidence at the Milosevic trial.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you. And in doing so, you recognised the fact that you were deceiving the Court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, sir, I explained to you a moment ago under which circumstances I testified. And then when I heard that Mr. Seselj and Mr. Milosevic would not leave this place alive, what else could I have done? I simply had to, along with the circus that was organised by Mr. Paolo Pastore. And Mr. Nice, when he came to Belgrade, he said, It's a good thing that you signed this statement. There are charges against you - against me, that is - and he said, These are irrefutable facts against Mr. Seselj. However, I had no chance to defend myself, and I had no one to turn to. Secondly, you took away all of my documents when I came to the Netherlands. I had no way of getting back to my own country.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Unfortunately, you have a pattern of not answering my questions. My question was a very simple one, and that was whether you recognised that you were deceiving the Court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was aware that it was an agreement, not that I was deceiving the Judges. How could I be deceiving Mr. Daniel Saxon when he taught me what I was supposed to say? As for the Judge, I hope I'm not making a mistake, it was Mr. May, he was the one who interrupted the proceedings if anything went wrong, if you remember the proceedings. On my right, I was looking at Mr. Daniel Saxon, who was nodding or shaking his head, depending on whether it was right or not. Who was I deceiving? I was deceiving Mr. Milosevic, if anybody, not the Court. That was the agreement as it was at the time, as I understand it. In my view, all of these charges were rigged. I'm telling you that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: We'll get to that in a moment. I would like to ask you a few questions about these signals that you talked about before. I had never heard of these -- of this allegation before, and I'm interested in getting a bit more detail. You said that there were signals that were exchanged between you and Mr. Saxon; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would look at him, and he would either nod his head or shake his head, yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: And when would he nod or shake his head; before or after you answered the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the answer. And I think that you have the recording, and you can see it. You can see where I looked and in which direction. That would be best, because that will confirm what I'm telling you now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Normally, when one thinks about signals, it's on the basis of a plan that was developed before. Did you have any discussions with anyone about the exchange of signals, including with Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: When did that take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During the proofing in the proceedings against Mr. Slobodan Milosevic, when he stated that Mr. Milosevic and Mr. Seselj would not leave this place alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: And what was the agreement that you say was developed between you and Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I've already said. I'm going to repeat it once again. I looked in the direction of the gentleman. I think he was sitting there. And after my answer, I would look at him, and he would nod his head, signifying that, Yes, you've said the right thing that you were supposed to say, and that was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Did you have any discussions with him after your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: And when did that take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the proceedings, after the proceedings were over. I mean, after my testimony, sorry, after I gave testimony in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: You, in your evidence, outlined a series of steps that some of the Prosecution investigators took, and you were critical of their conduct. You've said you didn't have anybody to speak to about it. Did you raise it with anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Why do you say "of course"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when I returned to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Who did you raise it with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I've already said, after my heart surgery, as soon as I got better three or four months later, I established contact with the Defence team of Mr. Vojislav Seselj in order to be able to tell the truth, to have someone to tell the truth to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: When did you first approach the Seselj team?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the 14th -- or, rather, the 19th of April, 2008. A day before that; say, the 17th. I don't know the exact date now. I do know when I gave the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: My understanding of the sequence is roughly this, and let me know if you agree with me: that your first statement to the Office of the Prosecutor was in July of 2002; the second was November of 2002; and that you testified in the Milosevic case in June of 2003. Does that sound right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The dates are right. I've explained that here. The first time was when Mr. Paolo Pastore took the statement. The second statement was when Mr. Nice came, and when he confirmed that these were irrefutable facts and that my indictment is not going to be activated. You are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Between your last substantial contact with the Office of the Prosecutor, through testifying, until the time that you approached the Defence, there is a lapse of about four years; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: I want to understand the sequence of events carefully. Your last substantial contact with the Office of the Prosecutor was through testifying in 2003, and then you approached the Defence in 2008; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: And you just said that the step that you took, as a result of what you thought was misconduct, was to approach the Seselj team. So it took you four years to do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I've repeated that a moment ago. Now you can tell me how a man who had open-heart surgery can contact someone even during the course of a year.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: I would just like to have an answer from you, though. It took you four years before you raised it with anyone, namely, the Seselj team; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm telling you, time and again, Mr. Paolo kept saying that I was in danger if I went back to Serbia, that they would kill me, that operatives were looking for me in the field. I arrived from Norway to Serbia in 2005 -- or, rather, to the border, where I was arrested because of this passport with a changed identity. You changed my identity twice, the first time in Holland, my first name and last name, and the second time in Norway. And of course they arrested me, because in my passport it said that I was banned from entering Serbia. Then I had heart problems, then I had open-heart surgery or, rather, stints first after the heart attack, and then constant problems until last year, the 19th of September, when I had an intervention yet again, again a stint implantation. You have all the medical documentation there. I submitted all the documents to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: You've gone quite far afield from my question, so I'll take your answer as a yes. I would like you to ask you questions concerning the statements that you provided to the Defence. It's my understanding that the first one was in April of 2008 and the second one was in August of 2008. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the Defence of Mr. Vojislav Seselj -- Dr. Vojislav Seselj. I gave the first statement on the 19th of April, 2008, and I would like to give it to you. This is the original that was verified in court. If you're interested, I can hand this over to you. It's my full name and surname, my pseudonym in the Slobodan Milosevic proceedings and in the proceedings against Mr. Seselj. That is the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: At the moment, I'm tracking through the sequence of events. It's my understanding that in October of 2008, you were directed by the Chamber to appear in this Tribunal in November, and you did not testify; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was undergoing this intervention then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: And I understand further that the same thing occurred a little bit later. You were ordered to appear in January of 2010, and you did not testify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, did you check what happened to me in January 2010? Do you know what happened to me then? I submitted to you documentation about that as well. There was this surgery at the Military Hospital in January, because, basically, I could not move for three months. I know that you were looking all over Serbia in hospitals for me. I know about that. Then in June, you issued this order, against my will, on pain of a fine of 100.000 dinars, so that my heart would be opened, against my will. And the surgery followed after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: I would like to get a few things straight, though. In responding to questions from Mr. Seselj, the accused here, you indicated that you would not want to testify on behalf of the Chamber; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't understand. I can be a witness only for the Defence of Mr. Vojislav Seselj -- Dr. Vojislav Seselj; nothing else. I can only be a Defence witness; nothing else. Everything else is out of the question, regardless of your threats and blackmail.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's just confirm, then, your position. You're saying you will not testify for the Prosecution, you will not testify for the Chamber; you will only testify for Mr. Seselj. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: You are, in essence --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There seems to be something wrong with this chair. Thank you. It's fine, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: I just want to confirm what I understand from you, sir: that you don't want to testify for the Prosecution, you don't want to testify for the Chamber; you only wish to testify for Mr. Seselj. Am I correct in saying that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct, and I would like to ask you to withdraw this indictment for revealing identity. The argumentation is here, facts that cannot be refuted, but nobody wants to look at this. Could you please take a look at what I've been telling you about?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: At the moment, I'm asking you questions, and I'm asking you to be responsive to my questions. You won't testify for the Chamber, you won't testify for the Prosecution; you will only testify for Mr. Seselj. I suggest to you that you have become a part of the Seselj team.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct. And I repeat, once again, exclusively for the Defence of Mr. Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: And as part of the Seselj team, you do not want to see anything adverse happening to Mr. Seselj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not part of that team. Mr. Seselj has his own team. Heaven forbid that something could happen to him. I just want him to come back to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Maybe there is something wrong with the translation, but I believe that two answers ago, in response to my question, you said you were part of the team.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, I said that I addressed the team for the Defence of Mr. Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: My suggestion to you, sir, is that while you might not be part of his expert team, you were a part of his supporters. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, in the future, if necessary. I am here to testify, to tell the truth, and nothing but the truth, in the case of Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: I ask you to answer my question, though. Is it not accurate to say that you're part of the supporters of Mr. Seselj?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, sir, the group that supports Mr. Seselj is about 3 million or 4 million citizens of Serbia, at least, who share my views and who feel the same way, if that's what you meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: And you're one of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you. You would not want to say anything in this chamber that would hurt Mr. Seselj; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
